questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A letter lock contains 5 rings each marked with four different letters. The number of all possible unsuccessful attempts to open the lock is
questions.solution:
Number of options on 1st ring $=4$
Number of options on 2nd ring $=4$
Number of options on 3rd ring $=4$
Number of options on 4rd ring $=4$
Number of options on 5rd ring $=4\therefore$ Total number of ways of all the options
$=4 \times 4 \times 4 \times 4 \times 4=1024\therefore$ Number of all possible unsuccesful attempts to open the lock is $=1024-1=1023$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The num of ways in which four letters can be selected from the word 'DEGREE', is
questions.solution:
There are 6 letters in the word 'DEGREE', namely 3E's and D, G, R. Four letters out of six can be selected in the following ways: (i) 3 like letters and 1 different, viz. EEE + D, G, R (ii) 2 like letters and 2 different, viz. EEE + any two of D, G, R (iii) All different letters, viz. EDGR
So, the total number of ways $={ }^3 C_1+{ }^3 C_2+1=3+3+1=7$

questions.solution:

Similarly, for two 2's... 9's

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The number of 4 letter word (with or without meaning) that can be formed from the eleven letters of the word 'EXAMINATION is .......
questions.solution:
Given word is 'EXAMINATION' having letters (AA), (II), (NN), EXMOT, we have to form 4 letter words, then following cases are possible,
(I) 2 same, 2 same and number of words are ${ }^3 C_2 \times \frac{4!}{2!2!}=18$
(II) 2 same, 2 different and number of words are
$\begin{aligned}
& { }^3 C_1 \times{ }^7 C_2 \times \frac{4!}{2!}=3 \times \frac{7 \times 6}{2} \times \frac{4 \times 3 \times 2}{2} \\
& =21 \times 36=756
\end{aligned}$
(III) All are different and number of words are
${ }^8 C_4 \times 4!=\frac{8 \times 7 \times 6 \times 5}{4!} 4!=1680$
So, total number of 4 letter words
$18+756+1680=2454$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Everybody in a room shakes hands with everybody else. The total number of handshakes is 66. The number of persons in the room is
questions.solution:
Let the number of persons in the room be $n$, then
$\begin{array}{rlr} & { }^n C_2=66 \\
\Rightarrow & \frac{n(n-1)}{2} & =66 \\
\Rightarrow & n^2-n-132 & =0 \\
\Rightarrow & (n-12)(n+11) & =0 \\
\Rightarrow & n & =12
\end{array} \quad(\because n \neq-11)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $N$ denotes number of 8 digit numbers that contains exactly four nines, then unit digit of $N$ is
questions.solution:
$N=$ Number of 8 digit number with exactly four 9.
$\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow N & =\text { Number with }\left[\left\{1^{\text {st }} \text { digit is } 9\right\}+\left\{1^{\text {st }} \text { digit is not } 9\right\}\right] \\
& ={ }^7 C_3 \cdot 9^4+8 \cdot{ }^7 C_4 \cdot 9^3 \\
& =9^3\left(9 \cdot \frac{7 \cdot 6 \cdot 5}{3 \cdot 2 \cdot 1}+8 \cdot \frac{7 \cdot 6 \cdot 5}{3 \cdot 2 \cdot 1}\right) \\
& =729 \times(315+280)=729 \times 595
\end{aligned}$
Hence, unit digit of $N$ is 5 .

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The total number of natural numbers of 6 digits that can be made with digits $1,2,3,4$, if all digits are to appear in the same number at least once, is
questions.solution:
There can be 2 types of numbers.
(i) Any one of the digits 1, 2, 3, 4 repeats thrice and the remaining digits only once i.e., of the type 1,2 , $3,4,4,4$.
(ii) Any two of the digits 1, 2, 3, 4 repeat twice and the remaining two only once i.e., of the type $1,2,3$, $3,4,4$.
Number of numbers of the type 123444
$=\frac{6!}{3!} \times{ }^4 C_1=480$
Number of numbers of the type 123344
$=\frac{6!}{2!2!} \times{ }^4 C_2=1080$
So, the required number $=480+1080=1560$

questions.q: In how many ways, can a student choose a program of 5 courses, if 9 courses are available and 2 specific courses are compulsory for every student?
questions.solution:
Total number of available courses $=9$
Out of these 5 courses have to be chosen. But it is given that 2 courses are compulsory for every student i.e., you have to choose only 3 courses instead of 5 , out of 7 instead of 9.
It can be done in ${ }^7 C_3$ ways $=\frac{7 \times 6 \times 5}{6}=35$ ways.

questions.q: A five digit number divisible by 3 is to be formed using the digits $0,1,2,3,4$ and 5 , without repetition. The total number of ways this can be done, is
questions.solution:
Since, a five digit number is formed by using digits $0,1,2,3,4$ and 5 , divisible by 3 i.e., only possible when sum of digits is multiple of three which gives two cases.
Case I Using digits $0,1,2,4,5$ the number of ways $=4 \times 4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1=96$.
Case II Using digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 the number of ways $=5 \times 4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1=120\therefore$ Total numbers formed $=120+96=216$

questions.solution:
Selection of 2 parallel lines from $m={ }^m \mathrm{C}_2$
Selection of 2 parallel lines from $n={ }^n C_2$
Hence, number of parallelograms $={ }^m \mathrm{C}_2 \cdot{ }^n \mathrm{C}_2=\frac{1}{4}(m-1)(n-1) m n$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In an election, number of candidates exceeds the number to be elected by 2. A man can vote in 56 ways. Then, the number of candidates is
questions.solution:
Let number of candidates be $n$. Therefore, $n-2$ are to be elected and so one can vote up to $(n-2)$. Hence, number of ways in which one can vote $\begin{aligned} & ={ }^n C_1+{ }^n C_2+\ldots+{ }^n C_{n-2}=56 \qquad \mathrm{(given)} \\ & \Rightarrow 2^n-\left({ }^n C_0+{ }^n C_{n-1}+{ }^n C_n\right)=56 \\ & \Rightarrow 2^n-n=58 \Rightarrow 2^n=58+n \end{aligned}$
Which is satisfied by $n=6$ only.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: 10 different toys are to be distributed among 10 children. Total number of ways of distributing these toys, so that exactly two children do not get any toy, is
questions.solution:
There may be two cases.
Case I. Two children get none and one get three and others get one each.
Then, total number. of ways $=\frac{10!}{2!\times 3!\times 7!} \times 10!$
Case II. Two get none and two get 2 each and the others get one each.
Then, total number of ways $=\frac{10!}{(2!)^4 \times 6!} \times 10!$
Hence, total number of ways
$=\frac{(10!)^2}{2!\times 3!\times 7!}+\frac{(10!)^2}{(2!)^4 \times 6!}=\frac{(10!)^2 \times 25}{(2!)^2 \times 6!\times 84}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: There are $P$ copies of $n$-different books. The number of different ways in which a non-empty selection can be made from them, is
questions.solution:
Number of selections of any number of copies of a book $=P+1$, (because copies of the same book are identical things). Similarly, for each book.
$\therefore$ Total number of selections
$\begin{aligned}
& =(P+1)(P+1) \ldots \text { to } n \text { factors } \\
& =(P+1)^n
\end{aligned}$
But this includes a selections which is empty $i e$, zero copy of each is selected. Excluding this, the required number of non-empty selections
$=(P+1)^n-1$

questions.q: The number of words (with or without meaning) that can be formed from all the letters of the word "LETTER" in which vowels never come together is___
questions.solution:
Given, word is LETTER, having vowels E, E and consonants $\mathrm{L}, \mathrm{T}, \mathrm{T}$ and R . Now, the number of ways to arrange the consonants are $\frac{4!}{2!}=12$ Now, we have five place to put vowels $E, E$.
So, number of ways to arrange vowels is ${ }^5 C_2=10$ So, number of required words $=12 \times 10=120$
